title: SourceHistoryRepository
responsibility: Lists the branches and commits of source history, leaving out evidence, notes and internal refs and marking commits kept only by an archive ref.

inputs.name: SourceHistoryRepository.constructor.root
inputs.description: The repository root path that the constructor passes to the GitAdapter it creates, and through which every git command of this repository runs. The constructor does not check the path; it only stores the adapter.

inputs.name: SourceHistoryRepository.read.limit
inputs.description: The most revisions that read returns; read asks git for one commit more than this so it can set truncated when history continues past the limit. The value is not validated.

inputs.name: SourceHistoryRepository.revision.commit
inputs.description: The commit to look up: any revision that git peels to a commit, such as a full or abbreviated hash, or a branch or tag name. It comes after --end-of-options, so a value that starts with a dash cannot be read as a git option.

inputs.name: SourceHistoryRepository.revision.branches
inputs.description: The branch names the caller already knows reach the commit; revision returns this list unchanged as the commit's branches and does not check it against the repository. An empty list makes the returned revision retained.

outputs.name: SourceHistoryRepository.read
outputs.description: Resolves to the branches (the local ones and those from remotes) and up to limit revisions, the commits reachable from the branch heads and archive refs in git's --date-order. truncated is true when more commits exist than limit, and a repository with no branch and no archive ref resolves with no revisions and truncated false.

revisions.subject: Record tested build for release candidate
revisions.author: Sam Okafor

outputs.name: SourceHistoryRepository.revision
outputs.description: Resolves to the commit as a SourceRevision, with its full hash and with branches set to the list the caller passed, or to undefined when the repository holds no such commit. Unlike read, it trims nothing itself: GitAdapter.attempt trims the whole output before it is split into fields, so subject loses any trailing whitespace.

examples.subject: Record tested build for release candidate
examples.author: Sam Okafor

errors.name: GitAdapter.run failure
errors.description: Rejects with the error the GitAdapter run call raises when one of read's git commands (for-each-ref, rev-list or log) fails; read does not catch it.
